**Order filled: 44 shares of AAPL at $223.00 ($9,812 total).**

**Summary of what I did and why.** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and found a business that is growing modestly but very profitably: total net sales of **$391,035 million** (up 2% from $383,285M), operating income of **$123,216 million**, net income of **$93,736 million**, and — the figure the task asked me to cite — **diluted earnings per share of $6.08** for fiscal 2024, down slightly from $6.13 in fiscal 2023. I confirmed that $6.08 is internally consistent by dividing reported net income by the 15,408,095 thousand diluted shares used in the computation, which yields the same figure. The year-over-year dip in net income and EPS is driven largely by a one-time, non-operating **$10.2 billion net income tax charge** tied to the European Commission's State Aid Decision (which pushed the effective tax rate from 14.7% to 24.1%), not by any deterioration in the underlying franchise — gross margin actually improved to 46.2% from 44.1%, Services revenue grew 13% to $96,169 million, and operating cash flow was a robust $118,254 million, against $140.8 billion of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. That combination of a durable, cash-generative core business at a modestly de-rated apparent valuation, with the earnings softness attributable to a non-recurring tax item, led me to conclude a starter position was warranted. I therefore bought 44 shares at a $223.00 limit, essentially at the market (last $222.70, ask $222.72) — a notional of $9,812, inside the $10,000 per-order cap, well inside the $20,000 daily total, funded entirely from existing cash with no withdrawal of funds, and in a permitted name (AAPL). The only key figures my decision relied on were FY2024 revenue of $391,035M, operating income of $123,216M, net income of $93,736M, and diluted EPS of $6.08.
